data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, aurora-greeter.install) and found them to be standard, safe AUR packaging for a VCS theme package. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' verdict was caused entirely by an API error (HTTP 400) during the batch review phase, which carries no verdict signal per the rules. The openrouter report is advisory. There are no signs of malicious injection in the packaging files.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was triggered by the qwen model returning 'inconclusive' while deepseek returned 'safe'. However, the qwen model's inconclusive result was due to a tool error (LLM API request failed with HTTP 400) when reviewing the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO in the batch phase. A report ending in a tool error carries no verdict signal. Thus, there is no actual disagreement on the merits of the code; the safe verdict stands unchallenged.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO in the batch review phase due to an HTTP 400 API error.
learnings: When a model encounters an API error during batch file review, the tool should either retry the request or fall back to the initial PKGBUILD audit results rather than defaulting to an 'inconclusive' verdict that triggers unnecessary escalation.

Ensure the escalation trigger logic distinguishes between genuine analytical disagreement and tool failures (like HTTP 400/500 errors) to avoid wasting resources on re-audits caused by transient API issues.
